title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Conflict of Interest - Family Member
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: A paralegal decides to represent their brother in a bitter landlord-tenant dispute against the brother's landlord. Because of their personal relationship, what specific duty must the paralegal be mindful of under the Rules?
options: The paralegal is strictly forbidden from representing immediate family members.

The paralegal must advise the family member that their personal relationship may interfere with the paralegal's professional objectivity, and should consider advising them to obtain independent counsel.
The paralegal must charge the brother double the normal rate to ensure professionalism.
The paralegal must report the retainer to the LSO.
questions.explain: There is no strict rule forbidding representing a family member; however, the LSO guidelines point out that personal relationships can impair professional objectivity (Rule 3.04). The practitioner must ensure they can represent the relative objectively, disclose the risk of lost objectivity, and often it is safer to advise the relative to seek independent counsel.
